grounds.point: M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd. has carried on business from the suit premises since 1997.
grounds.explanation: The respondent's pleaded position accepts that its two partners have also carried on business as directors of M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd. from the suit property since 1997, and the petitioner's submission identifies this operation as admitted. Section 14(1)(b), however, requires subletting, assignment or parting with possession, so another entity's business activity at the premises does not by itself resolve the statutory possession question.

grounds.point: Dhian Nath Kapur and Mrs. Anil Kapur are partners of the respondent firm and directors of M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd.
grounds.explanation: The respondent pleaded that the same two persons are its partners and directors of M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd., and it produced partnership material and a bank certificate concerning the directorships. This overlap is relevant to whether possession was actually relinquished to another entity, but the supplied record contains no withheld target-court finding resolving that issue.

grounds.point: The supplied record establishes that the respondent transferred exclusive possession of the whole or any part of the premises to M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd.
grounds.explanation: The landlord alleged that the respondent was no longer in possession and relied on the company's business operation, while the respondent maintained that its own partners remained in possession and continued the business. The reported Parasaram passage confirms that Delhi section 14(b) broadly reaches assignment or other modes of parting with possession, but the supplied material stops at the target court's formulation of this very issue and provides no finding establishing exclusive possession or an actual transfer on these facts.

grounds.point: The landlord gave written consent to the alleged subletting, assignment or parting with possession at issue.
grounds.explanation: The respondent alleged that the original landlord permitted Kapur family members to conduct business from the premises and relied on a 1964 rent receipt and related historical dealings, but the supplied descriptions do not identify a writing granting consent to the particular alleged subletting, assignment or parting with possession now in issue. Section 14(1)(b) expressly requires consent in writing, and section 17 likewise refers to previous written consent for post-Act subletting.

grounds.point: The supplied authorities establish that formation or use of a separate company by the tenant firm's same partners necessarily constitutes assignment or parting with possession under Delhi section 14(1)(b).
grounds.explanation: The original legal units establish the breadth of the Delhi provision and give distinct examples involving liquidation sale and company amalgamation, while the General Radio application arose under Andhra Pradesh law. Telesound expressly reserved the Delhi eviction consequence of amalgamation, and none of the supplied original legal units supplies a controlling rule that common partners/directors plus corporate business activity necessarily equals transfer of possession in the target factual configuration.

reason: Section 14(1)(b) would support eviction only if the tenant sublet, assigned or otherwise parted with possession without written landlord consent. The supplied record establishes another company's business activity and overlapping personnel, but leaves the decisive transfer-of-possession question unresolved, while the asserted historical permission does not establish written consent to the particular transaction; the fixed ground therefore remains undetermined on the allowed material. 粘贴的文本 (1)
